description:
Waluigi must document the sheer, unrelenting stubbornness of Archie Miser. And also the deeply suspicious architecture of how this ritual actually played out. Because it wasn't just recklessness. Something about this was WRONG in ways Waluigi is only now beginning to articulate.

Archie had just been informed that his magic bleeds entropy. He had just been shown that dimensional travel requires immense, agonizing power. He had just watched a man being ripped apart by crystal tethers.

His response? 'Enough dilly-dallying. Let's do the ritual.'

## The Time Dilation Problem

The Oracle revealed a critical piece of intelligence: Time is not synchronized across the planar fragments.

While only a few days have passed in the Material Plane, the Oracle explicitly stated that **A MONTH has passed in the Shadowfell**.

This is disastrous. Waluigi has been trapped in the Feywild. Waluigi does not know what the time dilation is there, but if the Shadowfell is moving at a highly accelerated rate, the geopolitical situation has entirely changed.

If a month has passed in the Shadowfell:
- Vivian Corvinarus has had 30 days to consolidate power or be hunted down.
- Green T has been surviving in a hostile, monochrome death-world for weeks.
- The Onyx Hand has had a month to recover from the Shattering of the Anchor and the shooting of Orangus Cornelius.
- Any rescue operation is arriving long after the trail has gone cold.

Archie didn't care. 'I still have to try. We haven't left a foot outside the mansion.'

Waluigi finds this admirable and MADDENING in equal measure.

## The Custody of Bones


Archie made one semi-responsible decision: he refused to take the comatose Bones through a volatile dimensional portal. He ordered the Oracle to watch over Bones, specifically demanding that the Oracle not subject Bones to his 'experiments.'

The Oracle agreed, stating it was 'quite a burden.'

Waluigi finds this arrangement deeply concerning. Leaving an unconscious friend with a 46-year-old interdimensional custodian who just showed you his secret room full of flesh vats is not a solid long-term healthcare plan. However, compared to taking Bones into a dimensional blender, it was the lesser of two evils.

Waluigi is choosing to believe Bones will be fine. Waluigi is not choosing this because the evidence supports it. Waluigi is choosing it because the alternative is too upsetting to document.

## The Ritual Setup — No Circle


And here is where Waluigi's first alarm bell rings.

The Planar Fracture — the original catastrophe that started all of this — required a ritual circle. Geometric patterns. Chalk and charcoal. Participant positioning across multiple designated anchor points. The circle was the INFRASTRUCTURE. It was how the dimensional mathematics worked. Without it, you weren't conducting a ritual. You were just throwing magical energy at a wall and hoping.

The Oracle lit candles. He instructed Archie to stand in the middle of them. He began to cast.

No circle.

Waluigi has been thinking about this since learning of it and Waluigi cannot stop thinking about it. The Oracle is a 46-year-old being — in Toad years, which compound differently than human years — who routinely manipulates space and time. He has a Planar Sanctum full of impossible equipment. He has flesh vats. He has rooms that Waluigi doesn't know about and probably doesn't WANT to know about.

Does the Oracle need a circle?

Or did the Oracle never need a circle?

The first ritual — the Raventree synchronization — used a circle because the PARTY built it. Multiple participants, distributed anchor points, geometric precision to compensate for what any individual caster couldn't hold alone. But the Oracle is not the party. The Oracle may be operating at a level of magical capability that makes circles redundant — the way a master carpenter doesn't need to measure twice because their hands already know the distance.

This would make the Oracle significantly more powerful than he has presented himself as being.

Waluigi is DEEPLY UNSETTLED by this possibility and intends to investigate further.

## The Anchor's Overload


The Oracle instructed Archie to stand in the middle of the candles. Archie was designated as the Anchor.

Waluigi has seen Archie act as an anchor before. It caused the Planar Fracture.

As the candles were lit, Archie began to absorb magical power to fuel the transit. The Oracle — a being who routinely manipulates space and time — looked at Archie wide-eyed and said, *'It may be too powerful.'*

Archie's response: *'Well, you'll be in Shadeward. Where in Shadeward? I haven't got a clue.'*

This is either Archie being brave or Archie not fully processing that 'too powerful' means 'this might kill you.' Waluigi suspects it is both simultaneously. Archie has a remarkable ability to be courageous and oblivious about the same thing at the same time.

## The Arrest — Everything Happening At Once


What the ritual entry would normally end here. Archie absorbs too much power, portal opens, Archie is fired into the Shadowfell, the end.

Except it did not end here.

Because while the ritual was building, the party outside was being rounded up.

The Toads — Lucky T, Regency forces — had been fighting Bystiall, who the party watched through a window earlier: a fire monster chasing Archie through the manor, Archie running upstairs, nobody noticing him. Standard Archie operational behavior. When the party caught up, they fought Bystiall and won. She knelt. She granted Regency full access to the manor.

The newcomer said: *'So you're the weak link then. The newbie.'*

Bystiall said: *'Ye — no. I'm not weak. I got captured on purpose.'*

Waluigi does not know if this is true. It is exactly what someone would say after being beaten. It is also exactly what someone would say if they had genuinely allowed themselves to be captured for strategic reasons. Bystiall's competence level is unclear and the distinction matters.

Then Berio arrived from behind.

*'We're not beating anyone,'* Berio said. *'It's Berio. Authorized to arrest.'*

Berio held Bones — still comatose — behind his back.

*'Time to round out all the Toads.'*

Lucky T, the Regency troops, everyone was quickly surrounded and taken. The operation was fast. Practiced. This was not improvised — Berio came with enough personnel and enough authority to sweep the entire exterior in minutes.

Then they went upstairs. Surrounded Archie. Asked him to sign a paper — a warrant authorizing search of the property. Everyone concerned about jurisdiction. The legal niceties of arresting a man in the middle of a dimensional transit ritual.

Archie, surrounded, absorbing too much power, candles lit, portal building behind him, said:

*'Fir—'*

Cut.

## The


Astral Altar — Where Waluigi's Problems Begin In Earnest

Archie woke in the Astral Altar.

Not the Shadowfell. Not mid-transit. Not the Planar Sanctum with a headache and singed eyebrows.

The Astral Altar. Crystalline structures around him. A warppad he didn't remember from the last time he was here. Darkness ahead.

And the Toad God standing before him.

*'So you come at last,'* the Toad God said. *'I had to wait for your friends to be occupied to bring you here.'*

Waluigi needs to stop here and be very precise about something.

The Toad God said *I had to wait for your friends to be occupied.*

The friends being occupied was Berio's arrest operation.

The Toad God waited for the arrest to happen. Then pulled Archie into the Astral Altar.

Which means either:

**A)** The Toad God was watching events at Raventree Manor in real time and seized an opportunity when Archie was isolated — the Oracle's ritual created a window and the Toad God hijacked it.

**B)** The Toad God knew the arrest was coming. Possibly arranged it. Possibly has reach into Berio's operations or the authority structure that sent Berio.

**C)** The Oracle's ritual and the Toad God's intervention are not separate events. The Oracle sent Archie somewhere the Toad God could intercept. Whether the Oracle knew this was happening, intended it to happen, or was himself maneuvered into creating the conditions — Waluigi does not know.

Waluigi is not comfortable with any of these options. Option A suggests the Toad God has surveillance capabilities that extend into the Material Plane in real time. Option B suggests the Toad God has political reach into Regency or Berio's command structure. Option C suggests the Oracle is either compromised or a participant in something much larger than a dimensional transit ritual.

All three options are bad. Waluigi is choosing to document all three rather than pretend one is clearly correct.

## The Toad God's Negotiation — A Summary of What Was Offered


The Toad God was cordial. This is perhaps the most alarming thing about him.

*'Hello, Toad Prime,'* Archie said. *'How's it going?'*

*'It's going well,'* the Toad God said. *'You haven't collected a single star shard yet and my plan progresses at a steady rate. Sooner rather than later the world will be mine.'*

*'Shame,'* Archie said. *'Good for you. My mind's not in a good headspace.'*

The Toad God noted he could simply kill Archie now. He didn't. Instead he made demands: Archie must be the one to collect the star shard. No one else. The Toad God wanted it specifically from Archie's hands.

The history between them was acknowledged. There is history. Waluigi does not have the full account of what that history is and finds this gap in his documentation UNACCEPTABLE.

The Newbee appeared — falling, crashing, landing badly. A lizardfolk. The Toad God identified him as a shard-holder who had gotten too close, too friendly with Archie's group. A problem to be disposed of.

Archie fired a freeze beam — ice, notably, not fire — and the Newbee tripped into a portal and activated it.

*'He got away, Mr. Miser,'* the Toad God said.

*'Do I have to chase him?'*

*'No, no. That's what mousetraps are for.'*

The Toad God offered Remi. Her eyes would be rotted to the core. Perhaps a third eye, like Archie's. A bargaining chip — here is something you care about, here is what I can do to it, here is what I want in exchange.

Archie thought about it for a moment. He did not care about Remi enough to make deals.

Waluigi is documenting this without editorial comment. Archie's emotional accounting is his own business. But Waluigi is NOTING it.

The Toad God offered the other path: bring it all back. Time reversal. The road not taken. Whatever was lost before all of this started, restored.

Archie pulled out his parchment. Drew the lizardfolk Newbee from memory — what he looked like, what he'd seen. Filed it away.

*'You'd rather fight me?'* the Toad God asked.

*'No,'* Archie said.

And walked away. Chose the path toward Shadeward Manor. Chose his friends.

## The Same Ritual,


The Same Destination, The Same Archie

Waluigi keeps returning to the parallel.

The Planar Fracture: ritual circle, multiple participants, Archie as anchor, reality shatters, everyone scattered.

The Shadeward Ritual: no circle, one caster, Archie as anchor, reality bends, Archie arrives in the Shadowfell — by way of the Astral Altar and a divine intervention.

Same ingredients. Same role. Same destination, eventually. But the MECHANISM was entirely different. The first time, the circle did the mathematics and Archie's unstable magic overwhelmed it. The second time, there was no circle, and the Oracle apparently held all the mathematics himself.

Which raises the question Waluigi cannot stop asking:

Was the circle ever load-bearing?

Or was the circle at Raventree a scaffold built for the party's benefit — a way of distributing magical work across multiple people who couldn't individually handle it — while the Oracle, alone, needed none of it?

And if the Oracle needed none of it, why didn't he simply send Archie to the Shadowfell from the beginning? Why the ritual? Why the candles? Why the performance of 'this is very difficult and requires preparation'?

Waluigi has theories.

**Theory One: The Oracle is genuinely more powerful than he presents.** The ritual was theater — not deception, exactly, but framing. The Oracle shows participants a process because it makes them feel involved and informed. The process is real in the sense that it describes what is happening. But the Oracle could skip it. He chooses not to because people trust what they can see.

**Theory Two: The candles serve a different function than the circle did.** The circle at Raventree was structural — a mathematical framework. The candles in the Oracle's ritual might be anchoring something else entirely. Focus. Direction. Archie as a specific kind of signal. Not 'here is the power source' but 'here is the destination marker.' The candles weren't building the portal. They were LABELING it.

**Theory Three: The Oracle knew the Toad God would intercept.** The ritual was designed to deposit Archie somewhere the Toad God could reach him — either because the Oracle is working with the Toad God, because the Oracle was maneuvered into creating that opportunity, or because the Oracle calculated that Archie going through that confrontation was NECESSARY and built the ritual to ensure it happened. The Oracle plays long games. Waluigi has no reason to believe this one was different.

**Theory Four: It wasn't the same ritual at all.** The Planar Fracture used dimensional synchronization — trying to align overlapping planes. The Shadeward Ritual was targeted transit — sending one person to one specific location. These are different operations that share only the anchor role. Waluigi has been treating them as comparable because they feel comparable. They may not be.

Waluigi does not know which theory is correct. Waluigi suspects elements of multiple theories are simultaneously true, because that is how this situation works. Nothing is one thing. Everything is several things at once.

## Waluigi's


Assessment

Archie Miser was fired out of a metaphysical cannon into a dimension that hates him, arriving a month late to a rescue mission, by way of a divine waiting room where a god offered him everything and he said no.

Waluigi wants to be angry about the recklessness. The ritual without preparation, the 'too much power,' the Oracle's wide-eyed concern. Waluigi has EARNED the right to be angry about this. Waluigi has been raising concerns about Archie's magical instability since before the Planar Fracture and nobody listens and things keep EXPLODING.

But.

The Toad God offered time reversal. He offered to bring it all back. He offered Archie a path out of this entire catastrophe, and Archie drew a picture of a lizard man he barely knew, said 'no,' and walked toward the Shadowfell.

Waluigi does not know what 'all back' means. Waluigi does not know what Archie lost, or what returning to before would have cost, or whether the offer was genuine or manipulation dressed as generosity. These are important questions that Waluigi intends to document when more information is available.

What Waluigi knows is this: when given the choice between power and his friends, Archie Miser chose his friends. In a world where everyone is making deals and calculating costs and deciding what they can afford to sacrifice, Archie looked at a god's offer and filed it under 'not interested.'

This is either admirable or catastrophically shortsighted.

Waluigi suspects it is both.

WAH.

description:
Waluigi has maintained throughout this encyclopedia that the Iron Legion and the Mages' Guild are corrupt. But corruption usually means taking bribes or falsifying documents. The Planar Sanctum proves that their corruption is metaphysical. They are quite literally mining human suffering to manipulate the fabric of reality.

## The Library of the Void


The initial arrival point was deceptive. A circular chamber with elaborately carved wooden shelves extending upward like stacked bands. Three grand lecterns in the center holding ornate, locked tomes. And directly overhead, a tiny aperture revealing a swirling starscape. 

Waluigi appreciates a good library. Knowledge is power, and power is leverage. Archie found a torn-out page referencing *Arcane Tethers, Planar Threading, Planar Resonance, Quintessence, The Weight of Time,* and *Accretion Sites.* This confirms that the Guild isn't just studying the Planar Fracture; they are actively trying to HARNESS it. They are treating the collapse of reality as a public transit project.

## The Grisly Tableau:


The Tethers

The illusion of scholarly tranquility ended when the floor shattered like fine china, ripping the royal purple carpet apart. (Waluigi takes personal offense to the destruction of royal purple carpet. Barbarians.)

Beneath the floor lay a grand central chamber open to the starfield. Two massive crystal formations were mounted in metallic casings:
- **The Western Crystal:** Thrumming with umbral violet energy.
- **The Eastern Crystal:** Flashing erratically with volatile orange energy.

These are the **Crystal Tethers**. And in the exact center between them lay a cracked metal tank. Behind the tank stood a man, silhouetted by lightning, enveloped by grasping tendrils of energy that seemed to rip and tear at him from both sides. 

Archie, demonstrating his usual lack of situational awareness, put his hand on the case and called it 'beautiful.' The Oracle corrected him. This is the agony that the Corvinarus curse inflicts. This man (likely a key figure of the bloodline, perhaps the original Orangus Cornelius or the architect of 'The Grafting') is acting as the living battery for the dimensional rift. Twenty years of agony to keep the planes tethered together.

## The Flesh Vats


If the Tethers were tragic, the adjacent room was an atrocity. 

A detached circular chamber drifting with centrifugal entropy. Inside were large glass tanks connected by thick pipes. Suspended within a glowing, luminescent fluid were humanoid bodies. 

They were malformed. Flesh open with weeping sores. Limbs ending prematurely. Metal tubes impaling their flesh and extending down their open mouths. Their eyes were open, but it was impossible to tell if they were alive. A disposal chute nearby indicated what happened to the 'failed' experiments.

This is what the Iron Legion and Mages' Guild are doing behind closed doors. They are not just treating prisoners as logistics; they are treating them as raw biological material for dimensional stabilization. The 'Somnium Captivus' that Bones is currently suffering from? It is likely the precursor to ending up in one of these tubes. 

The Oracle made it explicit: *'If we do the ritual, we won't have to end up in a vat like this.'*

## Waluigi's

Assessment

The Planar Sanctum is the dark heart of the Raventree Crisis. It proves that the overlapping dimensions are not just a magical accident; they are being actively, artificially sustained through horrific biological and arcane machinery. 

The Violet energy likely corresponds to the Shadowfell (Shadow Estate). The Orange energy likely corresponds to the Feywild (Overgrown Manor, the 'Orange Alignment' involving Hjumpik). The man in the middle is the anchor.

Waluigi has stolen from museums. Waluigi has rigged go-kart races. Waluigi has even scammed desperate Toads with useless corsets during a biological pandemic. But Waluigi has NEVER put a sentient being in a flesh vat to harvest their soul for a dimensional subway system. 

There is evil, and then there is *this*. The Iron Legion and the Mages' Guild must be dismantled. Not because Waluigi is a hero. But because Waluigi refuses to live in a universe where the ultimate authority is this utterly devoid of style and basic decency.

WAH.

summary: After beating the original Dan nearly to death in the Corvinarus Sanctum's collapsing library — confiscating his spellbook, photograph, wand, water pouch, and the Bowser Badge numbered 447 that had been fused to his skin and triggered partial immolation when removed — Bowser looked up and found Orange T already there. Orange T had been present the entire time, treating Bones in the corner with the comfortable familiarity of someone who had established routines, watching the fight with the disengaged attention of a man who was either supremely confident in his own safety or completely indifferent to the outcome. He greeted Bowser with 'you put on quite a show,' deflected questions about his own presence with 'I'm here now and that's what matters,' suggested Bowser had a mission involving other Oracles that Bowser knew nothing about, pointed at something invisible and laughed when Bowser could not see it, identified Bones as being 'from the future' while simultaneously dismissing him as 'no one important,' and then — in what Waluigi considers the most consequential casual question of the entire sanctum sequence — asked whether Bowser cared what he did with the two unconscious Dans. Bowser, exhausted and not thinking, answered: 'Not particularly.' Both Dans were immediately banished. Bowser objected only when the Shadowfell Dan was already disappearing, producing the specific variety of regret available only to people who realize exactly what they should have said at the precise moment when saying it can no longer help. Orange T said 'oh oops.' Waluigi does not believe the oops. They continued into the clockwork observatory — a mesmerizing catastrophe of bronzed wheels, interlocking gears, and slow-motion structural collapse that produced sustained gongs of embodied dread with each impact. At a gap in the floor, Bowser offered to throw the Oracle because he loves throwing Toads and they are kind of dumb. The Oracle objected to the dumb characterization. Bowser dismissed him as Mr. Magic Man and then punched the observatory floor to demonstrate his power. The floor cracked — under BOWSER, not the Oracle, which early retellings got wrong and which Bowser has been correcting with pointed personal investment ever since. Bowser fell into the void. He caught himself on a floating blue seat. The Oracle attempted to move the seat with a tuning fork. Nothing happened. Bowser accused smart people generally of playing with his feelings. He then deployed a Lakitu lightning rod to harvest ambient electricity, climbed into a Goomba Shoe, and bounced through the dying observatory squeaking with every impact while recommending the footwear to the Oracle as a purchasing opportunity. They reached a telescope platform. The Oracle offered Bowser a look. Bowser looked and did not see stars. He saw the Mushroom Kingdom after Peach's assassination — his own past self refusing to accept her death, threatening to burn things, watching Thornpaw arrive and deliver the Mages' Guild deflection, growing increasingly violent until Luigi arrived with guards and fought him with misdirection lightning and the Poltergust in full combat deployment. Bowser watched Luigi defeat his past self. He watched Toad guards drag his unconscious body away while Thornpaw conferred with two hooded mages and the guards informed his limp form that it was not authorized to know what was happening. Bowser pulled away from the telescope, called the vision 'something sad,' and continued into the sanctum. Waluigi notes that this is the fourth major surfacing of Bowser's grief over Peach during the Raventree operation, the first time he was forced to witness it from outside his own perspective, and also not the most damaging thing that happened to him in the sanctum, because the Shadowfell Dan is still gone. WAH.
description:
Waluigi has assembled this account from Bowser's retelling, which required the standard deflation process plus additional careful excavation of the moments where Bowser's account went quiet — because what Bowser does NOT say is usually more revealing than what he does. The Oracle's perspective has not been independently obtained because the Oracle communicates in the register of someone who decided long ago that direct answers are a form of weakness. Orange T's contribution to this account amounts to 'I was there and I did some things' plus a series of deflections that Waluigi found professionally insulting.

Waluigi has filled the gaps with analysis, inference, and the pattern recognition that comes from documenting this specific collection of catastrophe-generating individuals across multiple dimensional crises.

Waluigi must first issue a formal correction.

Early field reconstructions of the clockwork observatory sequence stated that the Oracle fell through the cracked floor when Bowser punched the ground. This is WRONG. BOWSER fell through the floor. Bowser punched the ground beneath his own feet, cracked his own footing, and dropped into the void below the observatory through a hole he substantially contributed to creating. The Oracle was standing approximately six feet away and did not fall. Bowser fell. Bowser caught himself on a floating blue seat. The Oracle then attempted to use a tuning fork to help, which is a different problem and will be documented separately.

Waluigi does not know why early retellings got this wrong. Waluigi suspects it is because 'Bowser punched a floor and fell through it' sounds like something that happens to Bowser, and 'Bowser punched a floor and the Oracle fell through it' sounds like something Bowser does TO someone, and the people relaying the story unconsciously upgraded Bowser's agency in the scene. Bowser himself has corrected this point in every retelling with unusual personal emphasis — not modesty, Bowser does not do modesty, but the specific insistence of someone for whom the EXACT sequence matters. It matters to Bowser that HE was the one who fell.

Waluigi suspects this is because falling through your own punched floor is funnier and more honest than accidentally dropping someone else, and Bowser prefers honesty to a flattering revision even when honesty is embarrassing.

The correction is now in the record. Bowser fell. Everything else proceeds from there.

Waluigi also wants to state something clearly before proceeding with the narrative, because the narrative contains a moment that Waluigi considers the single most consequential careless statement Bowser has made since the Raventree operation began, and that is a competitive field:

Bowser lost the Shadowfell Dan through a two-word answer to a casual question. 'Not particularly.' That is the sentence. That is the cost. Two words, spoken without attention, addressed to a question about two unconscious men on the floor of a collapsing room, and the result is that a party member who Bowser physically carried through a grove, rescued from a Mazebound in a literal tug-of-war, and protected through a fight with a Mages' Guild operative — that person is now banished to an unknown location in an unknown plane with no healer, no allies, and no idea where he is.

Bowser's grief over Peach, his fight with Luigi, his complicated relationship with intelligence and manipulation — all of this matters. All of this will be documented in full. But Waluigi will not allow the emotional weight of the telescope vision to obscure the fact that the Shadowfell Dan was lost before Bowser ever reached the telescope, through inattention and the particular exhaustion of a man who has been fighting continuously since he fell through a midnight portal and does not have the remaining focus to be careful with his words.

The telescope hurt Bowser. What happened before the telescope may have hurt someone else worse.

Waluigi documents both.

## Orange T:


The Toad Who Was Already There and Would Prefer Not to Explain Why

Bowser stood over the original Dan's body — beaten, cauterized, photographed, robbed of spellbook and wand and water pouch and the Bowser Badge that had been fused to his skin — and looked up.

Orange T was there.

Not arriving. Not entering. Already there, already treating Bones in the corner, already settled into the collapsing library with the comfortable familiarity of someone who had been in residence long enough to establish routines. Orange T occupied the Corvinarus Sanctum with the same energy that Green T had occupied the children's table at Orangus Cornelius's dinner — present in a space designed to make him irrelevant, positioned where powerful people would not think to look, and doing something more important than anyone watching would assume.

Waluigi does not know how long Orange T had been in the sanctum. Waluigi does not know how Orange T arrived. Waluigi does not know whether Orange T entered through the s

[... ADMINISTRATIVE PRUNING BY WALUIGI TO SAVE ARCHIVE SPACE ...]

o go? No wait, I am just visiting' — the grief is private. Not performed. Not defended against. Just present. The burn marks on the edges from drafts he almost destroyed and then kept because keeping matters more than quality. Bowser writes to Peach because stopping would require accepting there is no Peach to write to.

In the telescope, for the first time, Bowser watched his grief from outside it. He was the observer rather than the person experiencing the moment. He saw himself refusing the information. He saw himself threaten to burn something because burning was the only motion available when stillness was what the world demanded. He saw himself fight Luigi with a broken tennis racket from a match played before the world went wrong, because the racket was from a time when grief was not yet the context and carrying it into the hallway was a way of insisting the previous world still existed and could be returned to.

He saw himself lose.

He saw his body dragged across the floor by guards.

He saw Thornpaw talking to hooded mages while the guards told his unconscious form it was not authorized.

And he called it 'something sad' and kept moving, because that is the only thing Bowser knows how to do with things that hurt him.

Waluigi also documents the intelligence value separately from the emotional content, because both exist and both matter:

Thornpaw's presence and Guild deflection are consistent with the arrangement theory. He knew about the hatch. He directed Bowser away from the investigation and toward the institution controlling the investigation. His subsequent conference with hooded mages over Bowser's unconscious body is new data — not proof, but the kind of data point that fits a theory with aggravating precision.

Luigi's combat capability exceeds his documented profile. The misdirection thunder technique is designed strategy, not improvisation. The Poltergust's combat application sequence — strobe, taser, sustained illumination, capture function — is sophisticated multi-function deployment. The Luigi who takes bubble baths in haunted manors and picks locks with Iron Legion currency is also the Luigi who defeated a grief-empowered Koopa king through psychological misdirection and practiced tactical timing. Both are real. The gap between his public reputation and his actual capability is significant and getting larger as evidence accumulates.

Bowser's broken tennis racket as grief artifact: documented here because it belongs in the assessment and because it is the most human thing Bowser has done in the entire recorded history Waluigi has access to. He carried it from the match to the hallway. He used it in the fight he was conducting in the name of refusing to accept loss. The weapon he chose to fight with was the last object from the world that existed before everything went wrong. This is not strategy. It is the specific weight of things we carry when we cannot carry the actual thing we have lost.

But the assessment cannot conclude with the telescope. The telescope hurt Bowser deeply and produced intelligence of real value. The telescope is also not the worst thing that happened in the sanctum.

The Shadowfell Dan is missing.

The Shadowfell Dan was in Bowser's implicit care. Bowser had rescued him from a Mazebound in a literal physical tug-of-war, had carried him through a cursed grove, had protected him through a fight with a Mages' Guild operative. And then Bowser lost him through two words he spoke without attention to what they were consenting to.

The telescope showed Bowser being too late in 955 BF — arriving after the murder, unable to prevent it, dragged away before he could hear what was being said about what had happened.

In the Corvinarus Sanctum in 1040 BF, Bowser was too late again. Not because someone sent him away. Not because the conspiracy moved without him. Because he said 'not particularly' when he meant something more careful and Orange T used the imprecision as consent and the spell was cast before the objection could form.

Luigi hit Bowser through his laugh because Luigi knew Bowser would laugh when the fake thunder produced nothing.

Orange T banished the Shadowfell Dan because Orange T knew Bowser would say 'not particularly' when asked a question he was too tired to parse carefully.

Both were right. Both times, Bowser's predictability was the vector through which damage entered. The certainty that the fake thunder was the real thunder. The certainty that two unconscious people were not his current problem.

Bowser is learning things in this sanctum. He is learning them the way Bowser always learns things — through impact, through the quiet that follows impact, through standing in the echo of what just happened and deciding whether to call it a lesson or a failure. Usually it is both.

The Shadowfell Dan is somewhere in a three-plane system, alone, one-armed, with no idea where he is.

Bowser said 'let's go' and continued.

Waluigi continues to document.

WAH.

summary: Bones wakes up alone in the Fractured Planar Sanctum after the failed teleportation attempt with Archie. Stealing Fundamentals of Abjuration from the Oracle's collection, he discovers Corvinarus's ancient tome, Veins of the Tapestry, detailing 10 pages of critical planar history, the 988 BF Grafting ritual, warnings about the Oracle (OC), circle restoration instructions, and a dire prophecy. description:
Waluigi is documenting this incident with deep concern because Bones was left alone in the most unstable, vat-filled, reality-bending room in the entire Corvinarus Sanctum, and instead of taking a nap like a reasonable person, he started looting books and getting eaten by planar guard dogs. WAH.

## The Awakening &


The Grand Theft Abjuration
Following the shattered synchronization attempt with Archie Miser, Bones woke up alone on the cold, black marble floor of the Planar Sanctum within the Deep Mirror complex. The teleportation circle had failed—obviously—leaving him disoriented and isolated in the hum of an extradimensional complex. Sitting up and rubbing his aching head, Bones pondered his situation, asking himself, *"What should I do?"*

He remembered Thornbury Bones and began searching the immediate area for Archie Miser, privately assuming Archie had been swept away to the Shadowfell. Realizing he was completely on his own, Bones wondered aloud where the orange toad guy—Orange T—had vanished to.

While searching through the sprawling, crumbling library shelves, Bones spotted a heavy leather-bound volume: *Fundamentals of Abjuration* (the exact Mages' Guild Conservator volume recorded in archive indexes). Knowing full well that the book belonged to the Oracle, Bones picked it up, inspected its binding, and muttered to himself, *"When I get free time I'll keep it."* He pocketed the tome without hesitation. Waluigi respects the theft, though stealing from an entity who keeps human bodies in fluid tanks is the kind of risk assessment that makes Waluigi's mustache twitch.

## Corvinarus's Codex: Veins of the Tapestry

Walking further across the library floor, Bones stumbled upon a second open codex resting in the shadows: *Veins of the Tapestry: A Record of Threads Severed and Mended*, authored by Corvinarus himself in the precise, arrogant hand of someone who believed his bloodline could rewrite reality. Settling against the lectern near the ruined belfry—where the grand turret had collapsed, scattering rubble, furniture, and books across the marble floor alongside the fallen great bell—Bones read through the ten pages of the codex as memories whispered in his mind.

He read the chilling dedication on the first page, *"To the three who will break what we bound—may your hands finish what our blood began,"* signed with three interlocking threads, one already frayed. Flipped to the second page, he examined a pre-Fracture diagram of Raventree Manor marking mirrors and shadows as weak points, captioned, *"The house remembers its purpose even when the lords forget theirs."* Turning to the third page, he unraveled an account of the 988 BF Grafting ritual, which described the egg's scream as *"the sound of a future being forced into existence,"* set down in smeared ink.

On the fourth page was an explicit warning regarding the Oracle: *"She who calls herself OC pulls levers she does not fully understand.

The vats were never meant to birth keepers—only to hold them until the threads could be tested."* The fifth page cataloged a list of tested subject threads from Orangus Cornelius down to Vivian, where fresh ink noted, *"He laughs when cut.

This was not planned."*

Continuing through the volume, the sixth page detailed teleportation circle repair procedures requiring bone ash, live wood, iron dust, and chalk, accompanied by a margin doodle of a three-eyed staff-bearer cautioning, *"Do not trust the fire that cannot burn."* The seventh page recorded a Shadowfell branch lament, noting, *"Orangus believed order could contain the bleed. He was wrong. The Hand feeds what it claims to control."* On the eighth page rested a pressed Feywild flower carrying Lady Aurelian's recorded echo that *"the present must be severed from the others or all will unravel like cheap silk."* The ninth page provided a crude Deep Mirror map circling the vats as *"Failed attempts at continuity"* with *"Wrong lever"* underlined three times in the margin.

Finally, the tenth page ended mid-sentence with a prophecy fragment: *"When the one-armed shadow walks with the fire that bleeds, and the green one takes the children's table, the threads will knot or snap.

Choose the knot."*

Closing the volume in the belfry rubble, Bones thought to himself, *(Why do I feel called out in this book?)*

> **Waluigi's Structural Analysis:** Corvinarus named the entire current crisis in four phrases! The 'one-armed shadow' is Feyward Dan wandering with his severed arm; the 'fire that bleeds' is Archie Miser bleeding entropy; the 'green one taking the children's table' is Green T sitting at the kids' table during the vampire dinner in the Shadowfell! Corvinarus predicted Disaster Inc.'s seating arrangements eighty years in advance! WAH!

## Confrontation with the Oracle
Footsteps echoed across the marble rubble, prompting Bones to hide in the debris and peek out. Suddenly, the Oracle appeared behind him and asked, *"What are you looking at?"* Bones turned, apprehensive, and stammered, *"Woah, are we on good terms or what? I'm apprehensive right now."* The Oracle stared down coldly and reprimanded him: *"I gave you a simple task and you didn't even finish it, it's been two months since then, what's the hold up? Kill the other Oracles, free the planes..."*

Bones offered his apology, explaining, *"Sorry, after I woke up everything has been a blur to me. Archie seems to do what I had to do, how did I get here exactly?"* The Oracle rolled his eyes, stating, *"Let me check my book."* Glancing toward his shelves, the Oracle caught sight of his displaced collection and snapped, *"Don't touch my books... Listen... It's my stuff, if anything goes out of place here this place is already unstable enough."* Bones quickly agreed, *"I hear you, alright,"* wisely hiding the two stolen books tucked in his pack. When Bones inquired, *"What can I do for you?"* the Oracle bluntly replied, *"Hmm...

You can kill the other Oracles."*

## The Grand Central Chamber &

The Flesh Vat Offer
They proceeded into the heart of the complex, where all paths converged upon a grand central chamber whose solemn walls rose toward a roofless ceiling exposed to the open starfield sky. Dominating the hall were two massive Crystal Tethers mounted over deep floor apertures—a Western violet crystal thrumming rhythmically with umbral energy, and an Eastern orange crystal flashing erratically with volatile discharges. In the center lay a cracked glass tank, behind which a silhouetted man was bound as grasping lightning tendrils tore at him from both sides.

Bones pressed the Oracle: *"What's in it for me once we kill the Oracles?"* The Oracle answered simply, *"Closure."* Bones admitted, *"Closure... Yeah you're right, we have been around these manors for far too long. Will I get power?"* The Oracle smiled and promised, *"Yeah you will... We all will... Once we release the containment seals on these shards the vat will open and my true self reflection will shine."* Bones responded, *"Well alright, where will I go and who should I see where I am sent? Show me a picture."*

Before he could answer, a bell tolled and thunder struck through the chamber, forcing both to run. The Oracle shouted over the storm, *"How did you get the name Bones, what's your real name?"* to which Bones yelled back, *"I haven't thought of it!"* The Oracle ordered him, *"Quickly into the flesh vat!"* Recognizing the massive red flag of climbing into a vat of unknown fluid, Bones flatly refused and spotted an invisible portal opening nearby. As Bones attempted to flee, the Oracle seized him with telekinetic force and dragged him back, sneering, *"Where do you think you're going? If you're too weak to fight against the Oracle, you're too weak to fight against me!"* Bones conceded, *"Fine, let's fight whatever is here,"* making reference to fey swamps and the Feywild as he scooped up space-time floating rocks suspended in the air.

## The Canoloth Battle &


The Bare-Handed Drag
A hideous Canoloth materialized in the main chamber. Bones raised his ranged weapon and fired, but missed completely. The Oracle stepped forward holding a heavy, vibrating tuning fork.

> **Mordenkainen's Treatise on Yugoloths:** *"Canoloths are the preferred guard dogs of Yugoloth mercenary commanders... navigate legal loopholes... distortion field prevents dimensional escape... spiny tongues to grab their foes and drag them close."*

The Canoloth shrieked at the Oracle, who gripped his tuning fork and stepped back. The beast pounced directly onto Bones, coiling its spiny tongue around him and inflicting critical wounds. As Bones gasped in pain, the Oracle remarked dismissively, *"Woah... How did the situation turn south so fast? Maybe you're not fit to kill the other Oracles, Bones."* Bones swung his longsword at the beast, but his attack failed; the spiny tongue lashed outward, coiling tightly around both his longsword and his vile mace, pinning his arms in agonizing restraint.

Driven by raw desperation, Bones reached out and grabbed the Canoloth's spiny tongue bare-handed! The creature screeched in shock as Bones ripped his torso free—leaving his weapons entangled—and physically hauled the multi-ton yugoloth by its tongue toward the cliff edge. The Oracle shouted in disbelief, *"What are you doing? Throw it off!"* to which Bones growled back, *"No, kill it the actual way!"* In the next instant, the Canoloth lashed out with its razor-sharp claws, swiping across Bones's chest and knocking him unconscious.

## Interception by the Toad God at the


Astral Altar
Bones regained consciousness groaning in pain (*"Ugg... Oww..."*) upon the Astral Altar. Heavily wounded, he looked up to find the Toad God (Mad Toad) standing before him. When Bones asked, *"Who the heck are you?"* the Toad God claimed, *"Me... Your best friend."* Bones questioned, *"My best what?"* and the entity clarified, *"You wanted to go to Archie, right? I'm one of Archie's friends."* Skeptical, Bones remarked, *"Uhh, you're one of Archie's friends? I don't know, you're giving off a different kind of vibe... An 'itching to kill someone' vibe."*

Ignoring the suspicion, the Toad God offered guidance: *"Well whatever you think, I'll give you some advice."* Bones agreed, *"Alright,"* and the Toad God instructed, *"Don't kill the Oracle, keep him alive. Leave the manor and crystal shard intact and leave it divided."* Bones echoed the directives back to ensure clarity: *"Don't kill the Oracle, keep him alive, leave the manor and crystal shard intact and divided..."* The Toad God asked, *"You know what's going on, don't you Bones..."* and Bones replied, *"Yeah... What do you want from me, mad toad?"*

Offended by the epithet, the Toad God scoffed, *"I saved you and this is how you treat me? Maybe I'll send you back."* Bones frantically backtracked, pleading, *"You saved me? Sorry, sorry, sorry, don't send me back! ... I saved your life you accuse me of lying... You did, thank you... Despite being a survivor."* Satisfied, the Toad God explained, *"Well either way I don't want to show my face around, I've been too active of recent so you won't see me as much, as little as you have at least."* Bones asked, *"I hear you, what's kept you busy?"* to which the Toad God disclosed, *"Oh, you know, some pesky star bears wanting to give away their stars to a bunch of hooligans (the Oracle)."* When Bones pressed, *"Out of curiosity, to who?"* the deity answered evasively, *"Well let's just say they're a disaster, you wouldn't want to meet them now, chop chop."* Finally, Bones asked, *"How did you and Archie meet?"* but as the Toad God began, *"Well I first met by—"*, a blinding flash of light enveloped Bones and hurled him back across the void.

## Return to the Sanctum &


The Mental Fortitude Lecture
Bones awoke on the floor of the Planar Sanctum with the Oracle standing over him. The Oracle noted, *"See, I told you this place was dangerous. You were out for quite some time... An hour."* Bones admitted, *"Yeah I was."* The Oracle advised, *"Listen, take on people your own size next time, although I'm sure we could've taken him out together completely."* Bones remarked, *"You dealt with him? Oh who am I kidding, that is what happened. I tried to help despite how weak I was."* The Oracle reassured him, *"You still have a lot of potential Bones,"* before casting a restorative spell to heal his injuries.

When Bones inquired whether lifting weights would increase his combat strength, the Oracle delivered a stern lecture on psychological fortitude: *"Lifting weights won't make you stronger in the real sense, you have to mentally be stronger too Bones. You flinched at that monster, you ran away at danger, the flight or fight reaction was to flee. Being strong is fighting, not fleeing."* Bones argued back, *"Aah I already know that, and plus I thought I could have handled that thing, no one told me it was strong. Either way, we have to kill the Oracles right?"* The Oracle agreed, *"Yeah, it's party time."* Bones requested, *"Although teleport me to Archie pretty please, or a friend to either dimension."* The Oracle replied, *"Hmm oh a friend, I know who, I remember you mentioned them.

Okay, stand in the red circle,"* and activated a red teleportation circle that dispatched Bones across dimensions toward Mighdural in the Regal Capital.

summary: Bowser and the Oracle finally have the conversation the sanctum has been circling. It is not a fight. The Oracle fishes a boot out of nothing while explaining that a shepherd tends his garden; Bowser calls the sanctum a dumb space garden and demands to know why he is in the B plot. What follows is the most information the Oracle has ever surrendered in one sitting — that both Oracles are fated to die and he intends to be the last one, that the seals break and the world does not collapse, that he warned Peach and she did not listen because she may have wanted to die — and the most self-examination Bowser has ever done in public. Bowser refuses the Astral Shore trap on king's intuition, catches the Oracle spying on Peach through a floating eyeball, and negotiates: three weeks, not a cut tether, and he will personally keep the Legion off the Feyward. Then he steps onto the circle and lands alone in a basement where nobody is watching — a bowl of blood, a lever he does not pull, five labelled honeys, a knight's statue, a satyr running a bar for the Revel, and a room full of caged Goombas being shipped abroad for weapons by the Mushroom Regency. The Toad who owns the blood is Mystic Morel, and he leaves without explaining any of it. Bowser leaves his own countrymen in the cages. The clock starts when he lands.
description:
Waluigi has assembled this from Bowser's retelling, which arrived in an unusual condition: quiet.

Bowser does not do quiet. Bowser does volume, property damage, and the specific grammar of a man who has never once considered that a sentence might be improved by revision. What he brought back from the Planar Sanctum was a conversation he lost, a deal he made anyway, and a basement he walked out of without smashing anything. Waluigi has checked this account three times because it does not sound like the subject.

It is also, by some distance, the most the [Oracle](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/the_oracle) has ever said out loud.

## The garden

Bowser opened with the obvious question — why are you in this place — and got the answer that names the whole session: *a shepherd needs to tend to his garden.*

Bowser, who has more experience with hostile gardens than he would like, said it reminded him of the galaxy, back when he took over the Mushroom Kingdom for a second. He noted the absences out loud: no stars, no Rosalina. Then, because he is Bowser, he asked whether the Oracle had any stars.

The Oracle's reply was to cast a fishing line into the sanctum and pull out a boot.

Bowser's response to this was not anger. It was professional offence. *I'm the star of the show.* The Oracle told him he was relegated to the B plot. Waluigi wishes to record that a forty-something Toad custodian told the King of the Koopas he was a subplot, to his face, while holding a boot, and survived.

## The part where nobody is fighting

The fight never came, and by the end the Oracle said so directly: *you've gotten soft. I insulted you, I barred you, I even mentioned Peach, and you didn't attack once.* He added that half of what he said he did not mean, and hoped Bowser would not take it to heart.

He had been testing. The whole conversation was a measurement, and he told Bowser it was a measurement only after he had the reading.

Bowser's answer is the line Waluigi will be thinking about for a while. He looked down and said that after what happened to Peach, he has not been the same.

The Oracle: *we all change, don't we. We just don't all reflect on our actions. Some change for the better, some for the worse.*

## What the Oracle knows about the assassination

This is the section that will be cited.

Bowser caught him spying — a snap of the fingers and a floating eyeball appeared, which the Oracle had been using to watch the Princess. Bowser's objection was proprietary rather than moral: *only I get to do that.* He then declined to be angry at a little Toad, which is its own kind of new.

Asked why he cared, the Oracle said he wanted to know what drives a person to kill someone. And then he described the scene: five or six mages' locks broken. The room untouched. She sat there with a comb in her hand, dead, unmoving, the blood staining the floor. The guards came in. They all died, and the record does not say why.

Bowser: *you know something about her death.*

The Oracle: *yes. I know a lot of things. I ponder. I am the Oracle. I warned her. She ignored me — or maybe she didn't want to listen. She knew. She wanted to die.*

Bowser rejected it on the obvious ground: she had a kingdom to take care of, someone had to do it. And the Oracle asked the question that ended that line of argument — *was it really her kingdom, or the Mushroom Kingdom?*

Waluigi is not going to pretend to be neutral about this. An unbroken room, broken locks, a comb still in her hand, and a full guard detachment dead of no stated cause is not a description of a murder. It is a description of a scene someone arranged to be read. The Oracle has been holding this for the entire operation and gave it up in a room with no witnesses, to a man he had spent the previous hour needling into stillness.

## The trap Bowser did not walk into

The Oracle offered to send Bowser directly to the Oracle — the other one — at a place called the Astral Shore, where Bowser *may kill* him. Bowser asked whether [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) would be there. The Oracle smiled and said yes, he'll be there.

Bowser did not take it. His exact objection is a better piece of analysis than most of what this archive produces:

> In what way? Like, is he *present*? You Toads are very puzzly. You hide your intentions.

The Oracle's clarification confirmed the suspicion: Hjumpik would be there in the same way that it is fate for both Oracles to die and for him to become the sole Oracle. No more orbiting. No more watching. A prophecy, not a promise, and a prophecy will happily be satisfied by a corpse.

Bowser asked what the Oracle got out of it. The answer was three things and Waluigi believes two of them: the seals break, the world does not collapse, and Bowser gets to go home away from him.

Then: *something tells me Hjumpik isn't there. Call it king intuition.* And: *you're trying to trap me and I don't like being tricked.*

He demanded the power star and no more lying.

Waluigi wants the record to show that Bowser was offered a shortcut to the thing he wants, spotted it was rigged from a single evasive verb tense, and said no. *If I was that dumb, I wouldn't be a king.*

## The deal

The Oracle wanted blood inside one week or he would manually cut the planar tether linking the Feyward to the Material sanctum. Bowser countered.

The negotiation, in order: Bowser asked for three weeks, on the grounds that these guys are slow. He argued that Hjumpik avoids fights and talks — *he loves to talk, talk, talk* — so two or three weeks is realistic and four is the failure case. He offered something better than a deadline: rather than the Oracle cutting the plane, Bowser would personally make sure it does not get too rowdy with the Iron Legion, and if he is going down he wants to go out on his own terms, not because of his companions.

He asked for one specific concession and repeated it twice: **do not cut it exactly at three weeks.** Give him a margin. *I want some insurance, Mr. Self-Reflection, if that's fine.*

The Oracle's counter-offer was three surprises waiting if Bowser makes it: one that smells like peaches, one involving arts and crafts, and one that is something Bowser wanted today.

Bowser heard *peaches* and did not get angry, and did not let himself hope. His line — *I don't know if this is a test or get hopes up* — is the most guarded sentence in his file.

There was also a live objection that the archive should not lose: Bowser asked whether they had to kill the Oracles at all, since Hjumpik had said he wanted to talk to them. That objection came from Bowser. It is on the record.

**The clock starts on teleport.** Three weeks. The Oracle started it as Bowser stepped onto the circle.

## The basement

He landed alone.

A sigil carved in the floor. A table, a bowl of blood, candles lighting the room warmly. Above him, muffled, the Revel; around him, the clear sound of dripping water. And a lever on the wall which Bowser described as *begging to be touched.*

He did not pull it. Waluigi has read this line four times and it still does not sound like the subject of this file. *My workplace. I don't have time to be wasting.*

What followed is a solo infiltration by a man with no subtlety and a functioning sense of priority. He stepped off the altar. He passed the crest of Raventree on a shield, walked over bones and candles, and thought — *I think I was there* — which is the first indication in the record that Bowser recognises this estate.

He failed to pick a lock because his hands are too big. He found cold storage and five labelled honeys. And then, from behind him, a voice with an opinion about preserves.

## The Toad in the cellar

One Toad is in this basement, and the archive should be precise about him, because he already has a record and a habit of being underestimated.

**[Mystic Morel](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mystic_morel) — Purple T** — is the one who appears behind Bowser. Not arriving; already there, with an opinion about preserves: *I prefer jam.* Bowser asked who he was. He denied being an Oracle, introduced himself as a friend of Hjumpik, and stopped caring the moment Bowser proved not to be a newcomer.

He is also the one who owns the bowl of blood on the altar table. *Not my blood, but yeah, it's mine.* He asked whether Bowser had touched anything in that room, said he had been using it, wished him the best of luck, and left. The door slammed. Bowser took the honey.

Between them the session learned more about Bowser than about the Toad. On [Archie](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/archie_miser): a destructive force, a headache, wanted by the Mages' Guild, and *kinda crazy* — not a random magic user. The reply was indifference. On the fireballs: *it reminds me of me, back in the day.* Asked why he stopped, Bowser gave an answer he has never given in this archive before — an incident happened with a kingdom, he slowed down, he started to realise life isn't about throwing fireballs, he lost his purpose in an instant, and he is here for vengeance. The Toad said they shared that goal.

The terms were set from the other side: *as long as you don't get in my way, you're NOT an enemy.*

And on Hjumpik, Bowser said the quiet thing: he would have made a good frontliner in one of his kingdom battles. He talks too much. **Not a friend — but I like him more than the rest of my dumb group.**

Asked why he had not allied with more Koopas, Bowser said his men have to take care of his kingdom while he is gone, and that he misses his Koopas. His children.

Waluigi is going to leave that sentence sitting next to the next section without comment for exactly one paragraph.

## The cages

Bowser was called over by a goblin to help move cargo. He asked where he was and what the time was, and got the answer this filing cannot resolve: *722? Maybe like 2 AM.* The Oracle had said 922. Bowser said *722, right, okay* and moved on.

He asked which castle he was in and was corrected: it is not a castle, it is a mansion, and he is in the **Cornivours estate**. The goblin found his confusion suspicious — *are you not meant to be here?*

Bowser deflected into the job. Then the handler called him a Goomba.

*Who are you calling a Goomba? Show me the Goomba.*

The handler brought out a cage. Asked who was in it, he said: *I don't know. Food?*

The cargo is Goombas. Nine of them, in cages, stacked. Bowser asked where they came from and who sent them, and got the shape of an answer that reframes the entire operation: there was an ambush, there is a whole food chain, and **the Mushroom Regency is shipping people off to other countries for weapons.**

Bowser's reaction to a sentient-trafficking pipeline run by the Regency was to declare it could not be tolerated and that he would deal with them later. Waluigi notes that this is the King of the Koopas taking a firmer public line on Regency conduct than the Regency's own opposition has managed this year.

Then he asked whether any of them had sold information, threatened to smash one that hesitated, and left them in the cages.

His stated reason: they are meant to be his men, getting caught brings his kingdom's reputation down, and they are dumb for getting caught. He will figure out what to do with them later. He does not want them getting stopped the way Mario did.

Waluigi has been documenting Bowser for a long time and this is the single most Bowser sequence in the file. He identified an atrocity, condemned it correctly, committed to acting on it eventually, and then left the victims in the cage because letting them out would be a bad look. He misses his children. He walked past nine of his own countrymen in a shipping crate and pulled the door shut behind him.

## The satyr, and the chest that held

Past the cages: a satyr playing cards against himself, who has not been outside much and is not a fan of the Revel but keeps the drinks going up to it. Bowser asked after Hjumpik and a dwarf and got a ruckus outside and nothing more.

They played. The record shows two hands, both wins, both bet 25 — dealer busts, player holds 19, then 20.

The satyr's intelligence is better than his card play. Asked who his boss was, he ruled out the Revel with genuine disgust — *that pile of fleshy, mouldy thing? How could it even speak? It just eats and eats and eats* — and named the **Orange Heir**, who is organising an army of tree-cutters to fight the overgrowth. A green hag walked in, mocked Bowser's own question back at him in his own voice, and the door closed.

Bowser asked what was in the chests. Personal mementos, supplies, people's beds. He was handed a jug and told it could be filled on the way out, possibly to get someone drunk.

He punched the chest anyway. The chains rattled. He punched it again. The chains held.

Waluigi records this as the session's only honest defeat: a man who cracked the floor of a clockwork observatory with one punch could not open a cellar footlocker, twice.

## Standing

Bowser is in the Feyward basement with a jug, five honeys, a door knob, and three weeks. Hjumpik does not know he is coming. The party above does not know the tether has a deadline on it. The Oracle is counting.

WAH.

THE YEAR IS DISPUTED: the Oracle says 922, the goblin says '722? maybe like 2 AM', and Bowser accepts 722 without resolving it
The estate is named on site as the Cornivours estate; the shield in the hall carries the crest of Raventree

reputationNotes.bowser: Negotiated a planar deadline up from one week to three without conceding the kill, refused a rigged shortcut, and took a public position against the Mushroom Regency's trafficking pipeline — then left nine of his own countrymen in the cages, which the archive records alongside the position rather than behind it.
reputationNotes.the_oracle: Disclosed more than at any prior point in the operation, including the assassination scene and his own intention to become the sole Oracle, and admitted the conversation was a test.
reputationNotes._record: The Mushroom Regency is now on the record, via a goblin freight handler in another plane, as shipping sentient people abroad in exchange for weapons. The claim is uncorroborated and comes from a hostile source under no obligation to be accurate, but it is specific and it names a mechanism.

aftermath:
**Standing.** A hard three-week countdown is running on the planar tether between the Feyward and the Material sanctum; it started the moment Bowser teleported. Bowser is in the Feyward basement alone, carrying five honeys, a jug, and a door knob. Hjumpik and the Feyward party do not know the clock exists, do not know Bowser is beneath them, and are three sessions into their own operation upstairs. The Oracle is counting and has promised three unnamed rewards if the deadline holds. Nine Goombas remain caged as freight. The Orange Heir is raising a tree-cutting army. The satyr's chest is still shut.

**Unresolved.** The basement's year: the Oracle said 922, the goblin said 722, and nobody settled it. The archive files both readings rather than pick one.
waluigiAssessment:
Waluigi wants to isolate the thing that actually happened here, because the session looks like a negotiation and is in fact an audit of Bowser conducted by a Toad with a fishing rod.

The Oracle insulted him, barred him, dangled a shortcut, and named Peach — the one subject that has reliably produced property damage for eighty-five years. Bowser did not swing. At the end the Oracle said so out loud, which means the entire exchange was instrumentation and the reading was taken before Bowser knew he was being read. He was measured, and he passed a test whose passing condition was restraint.

And Bowser knew he was being handled and made the deal anyway, because the deal was better than the ultimatum. One week became three. A cut tether became a margin he asked for twice. That is not a man being outplayed. That is a man who understands he is the weaker party at the table and is negotiating competently from there.

Then there is the assassination. Waluigi has been building this file for a long time and has never had a witness say *I warned her.* An untouched room behind five or six broken mages' locks, a comb still in her hand, and every responding guard dead with no cause recorded. That is not a killing. That is a composition. Someone wanted the room to be read a particular way, and the Oracle — who watches, who ponders, who admits to a floating eyeball over the Princess — is now the closest thing this archive has to a source who was paying attention at the time.

Waluigi does not believe the Oracle is telling the truth. Waluigi believes he is telling *a* truth, selected, on purpose, to a man he had just finished measuring.

And then the cages.

Waluigi is not going to be delicate about this section. In the same hour, Bowser said he misses his Koopas and called them his children; identified a Regency pipeline shipping sentient people abroad for weapons; correctly called it intolerable; and walked away from nine of them in a crate because being captured makes his kingdom look bad. All four of those are true at once. That is the character. Not a hypocrite discovering himself — a man whose loyalty runs exactly as deep as his reputation requires and stops precisely there.

He did not pull the lever. He could not open the chest. He left his countrymen in the cages, and he has three weeks.

WAH.
