imageCaption: The Planar Sanctum, mid-negotiation. Bowser with both arms out demanding to know why he is in a dumb space garden; the Oracle seated on a floating slab with a fishing rod, having just pulled a sodden boot out of the void. The size difference is the whole conversation: the small calm one set the terms.

sections.name: The Garden and the Boot
sections.subtitle: a shepherd tends his garden, and the star of the show is informed he is a subplot
sections.overview:
Bowser asked the obvious question and got the answer that names the session: *a shepherd needs to tend to his garden.*

He said it reminded him of the galaxy, back when he took over the Mushroom Kingdom for a second, and noted the absences out loud — no stars, no Rosalina. Then he asked whether the Oracle had any stars.

The Oracle cast a fishing line into the sanctum and pulled out a boot.

Bowser's response was not anger. It was professional offence: *I'm the star of the show.* The Oracle told him he was relegated to the B plot.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* A forty-something Toad custodian told the King of the Koopas he was a subplot, to his face, while holding a wet boot, and is still alive. Waluigi has seen people lose limbs for less and wants that on the record.
sections.imageCaption: The negotiation, accurately staged. Bowser with both arms out demanding to know why he is in a dumb space garden; the Oracle seated on a floating slab with a rod, having just landed a boot. The size difference is the whole conversation — the small calm one set the terms.

sections.name: The Test Nobody Told Him About
sections.subtitle: an hour of deliberate provocation, and the one time Bowser did not swing
sections.overview:
The fight never came, and at the end the Oracle said why: *you've gotten soft. I insulted you, I barred you, I even mentioned Peach, and you didn't attack once.* He added that half of what he said he did not mean.

He had been measuring. The entire exchange was instrumentation, and Bowser was told only after the reading was taken.

Bowser's answer is the quietest line in his file. He looked down and said that after what happened to Peach, he has not been the same.

The Oracle: *we all change, don't we. We just don't all reflect on our actions. Some change for the better, some for the worse.*
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Waluigi has documented this subject through four dimensional crises and has never once seen him absorb the name Peach without breaking something. He absorbed it here, from a man who said it on purpose to see what would happen.

sections.name: What the Oracle Knows About the Assassination
sections.subtitle: five or six broken locks, an untouched room, and a comb still in her hand
sections.overview:
Bowser caught him spying. A snap of the fingers and a floating eyeball appeared — the Oracle had been watching the Princess with it. Bowser's objection was proprietary rather than moral: *only I get to do that.*

Asked why he cared, the Oracle said he wanted to know what drives a person to kill someone. Then he described the scene.

Five or six mages' locks broken. The room untouched. She sat there with a comb in her hand, dead, unmoving, the blood staining the floor. The guards came in. They all died, and the record does not say why.

> *Yes. I know a lot of things. I ponder. I am the Oracle. I warned her. She ignored me — or maybe she didn't want to listen. She knew. She wanted to die.*

Bowser rejected it: she had a kingdom to take care of, someone had to do it. The Oracle ended that line with a question — *was it really her kingdom, or the Mushroom Kingdom?*
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Waluigi is not neutral here. Broken locks, an unbroken room, a comb still in her hand and a full guard detachment dead of no stated cause is not a description of a murder. It is a description of a scene arranged to be read. And the only witness willing to discuss it is a man who admits to keeping an eyeball over her.

sections.name: The Astral Shore, Declined
sections.subtitle: a shortcut to the thing he wants, refused over one evasive verb
sections.overview:
The Oracle offered to send Bowser straight to the other Oracle, at a place called the Astral Shore, where he *may kill* him. Bowser asked whether Hjumpik would be there. The Oracle smiled: yes, he'll be there.

Bowser did not take it.

> In what way? Like, is he *present*? You Toads are very puzzly. You hide your intentions.

The clarification confirmed it: Hjumpik would be there in the same way that it is fate for both Oracles to die and for this one to become the sole Oracle. No more orbiting. No more watching. A prophecy, not a promise — and a prophecy is satisfied just as well by a corpse.

Asked what he got out of it, the Oracle named three things: the seals break, the world does not collapse, and Bowser gets to go home away from him.

> Something tells me Hjumpik isn't there. Call it king intuition.

He demanded the power star and an end to the lying. *If I was that dumb, I wouldn't be a king.*
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Waluigi wants this filed prominently, because the archive has spent years describing this man as a blunt instrument. He was handed the shortest route to his own objective, detected the trap in a verb tense, and walked away from it.

sections.name: Three Weeks
sections.subtitle: the clock starts on teleport, and he asked twice for a margin
sections.overview:
The Oracle wanted blood inside one week, or he would manually cut the planar tether joining the Feyward to the Material sanctum. Bowser countered.

He asked for three weeks, on the grounds that these guys are slow. He argued Hjumpik avoids fights and talks — *he loves to talk, talk, talk* — so two or three weeks is realistic and four is the failure case. Then he offered something better than a deadline: instead of the Oracle cutting the plane, Bowser personally keeps the Iron Legion off the Feyward, and if he goes down he goes out on his own terms rather than through his companions.

He asked for one concession, twice: **do not cut it exactly at three weeks.** Give him a margin.

The counter-offer was three surprises if he makes it — one that smells like peaches, one involving arts and crafts, and one that is something Bowser wanted today.

He heard *peaches* and did not get angry, and did not let himself hope: *I don't know if this is a test or get hopes up.*

One more thing belongs in the record. Bowser asked whether they have to kill the Oracles at all, since Hjumpik had said he wanted to talk to them. **That objection came from Bowser.**
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* One week became three. A severed plane became a margin he had to ask for twice. That is not a man being outplayed — that is a man who knows he is the weaker party and negotiates properly from there. The clock starts on the teleport, not on the handshake.

sections.name: The Basement Nobody Was Watching
sections.subtitle: a bowl of blood, a lever, and the honey
sections.overview:
He landed alone. A sigil carved in the floor, a table, a bowl of blood, candles lighting the room warmly. Above him the muffled Revel; around him the clear sound of dripping water. And a lever on the wall which Bowser described as *begging to be touched.*

He did not pull it. *My workplace. I don't have time to be wasting.*

He stepped off the altar, passed the crest of Raventree on a shield, walked over bones and candles, and thought — *I think I was there* — the first sign in the record that he recognises this estate. He failed to pick a lock because his hands are too big. He found cold storage and five labelled honeys: Warrior, Norn-Blessed, Hearth Fire, Hive Warden, Sacred Bear.

Then, from behind him, a voice with an opinion about preserves.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Waluigi has read the lever sentence four times. A wall lever, unlabelled, in a room he had just been deposited in by a man he does not trust, and he left it alone. Growth is a horrible thing to witness.

sections.name: The Toad Who Was Already Behind Him
sections.subtitle: Purple T claims the blood, denies being an Oracle, and answers nothing
sections.overview:
There is one Toad in this basement, and he is already behind you.

**Mystic Morel — Purple T** — spoke from behind Bowser while Bowser was inspecting the cold storage. His opening contribution was a correction about preserves: *I prefer jam.* Bowser asked who he was. He denied being an Oracle, introduced himself as a friend of Hjumpik, and lost interest the moment Bowser proved not to be a newcomer — *oh, thought you were a newcomer. What are you doing down here, come to stop me?*

He is also the one who owns the bowl of blood on the altar table. *Not my blood, but yeah, it's mine.* He asked whether Bowser had touched anything in that room, was told no, said he had been using it, wished him the best of luck and left. The door slammed. Bowser took the honey.

Between the two of them the session learned far more about Bowser than about the Toad. On Archie: a destructive force, a headache, wanted by the Mages' Guild, *kinda crazy* — not a random magic user. The reply was indifference. On the fireballs: *it reminds me of me, back in the day.* Asked why he stopped, Bowser gave an answer he has never given in this archive before — an incident with a kingdom, he slowed, he started to realise life isn't about throwing fireballs, he lost his purpose in an instant, and he is here for vengeance. The Toad recognised a shared goal and said so.

Then the terms, from his side: *as long as you don't get in my way, you're NOT an enemy.*

And on Hjumpik, Bowser said the quiet thing: he would have made a good frontliner in one of his kingdom battles. He talks too much. **Not a friend — but I like him more than the rest of my dumb group.**
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Note the precision of the Toad's sentence. Not 'you are a friend.' Not even 'we are allies.' A conditional absence of hostility, with the condition stated first. Waluigi has read contracts with more warmth. And note what he never answered: what the blood is for, what he was using the room for, or why a fortune teller who robs people is standing in the Feyward with a bowl of it.

sections.name: The Cages
sections.subtitle: nine Goombas, a weapons trade, and the door he pulled shut behind him
sections.overview:
A goblin called him over to move cargo. He asked where he was and what the time was, and got the answer this filing cannot resolve: *722? Maybe like 2 AM.* The Oracle had said 922. Bowser said *722, right, okay* and moved on.

He asked which castle he was in and was corrected: not a castle, a mansion — the **Cornivours estate**. The goblin found his confusion suspicious.

Then the handler called him a Goomba. *Who are you calling a Goomba? Show me the Goomba.*

The handler brought out a cage. Asked who was inside, he said: *I don't know. Food?*

The cargo is Goombas. Nine of them, stacked. Bowser asked where they came from and who sent them, and got the shape of an answer that reframes the whole operation: there was an ambush, there is a whole food chain, and **the Mushroom Regency is shipping people off to other countries for weapons.**

Bowser declared it could not be tolerated and that he would deal with them later. He asked whether any of them had sold information, threatened to smash one that hesitated — and left them in the cages.

His reasons: they are meant to be his men, getting caught brings his kingdom's reputation down, they are dumb for getting caught, and he does not want them getting stopped the way Mario did.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* In the same hour he said he misses his Koopas and called them his children. Then he identified a Regency pipeline trading sentient people for weapons, called it correctly, and walked past nine of his own countrymen in a crate because letting them out would look bad. All of that is true at once. That is not a hypocrite discovering himself — that is a man whose loyalty runs exactly as deep as his reputation requires and stops precisely there.
sections.imageCaption: The last look. Nine Goombas held as freight in a Feyward cellar, and the King of the Koopas leaving — head turned back over his shoulder, jaw set, already walking. He called the trade intolerable on his way out.

sections.name: The Satyr, and the Chest That Held
sections.subtitle: cards, the Orange Heir, and the session's only honest defeat
sections.overview:
Past the cages: a satyr playing cards against himself, who does not go out much and is not a fan of the Revel but keeps the drinks going up to it. Bowser asked after Hjumpik and a dwarf, and got a ruckus outside and nothing more.

They played two hands, both bet 25, both wins — dealer busts against 19, then 20.

The satyr's intelligence is better than his card play. Asked who his boss was, he ruled out the Revel with real disgust — *that pile of fleshy, mouldy thing? How could it even speak? It just eats and eats and eats* — and named the **Orange Heir**, who is organising an army of tree-cutters against the overgrowth. A green hag walked in, mocked Bowser's own question back at him in his own voice, and the door closed.

The chests hold personal mementos, supplies, people's beds. Bowser was handed a jug and told it could be filled on the way out, possibly to get someone drunk.

He punched the chest anyway. The chains rattled. He punched it again. The chains held.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* A man who cracked the floor of a clockwork observatory with one punch could not open a cellar footlocker in two. Waluigi is choosing to find this funny because the alternative is thinking about the cages again.
